introduction: Today we celebrate the Most Holy Trinity. The Book of Proverbs speaks of Wisdom, present with God at the creation of the world, delighting in the human race. Paul tells us that we have peace with God through Christ, and that God's love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit. Jesus promises that the Spirit will guide us into all truth. Let us adore the one God, Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

prayerOfTheFaithful.invitation: Brothers and sisters, God's love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit. Let us pray to the Father, through the Son, in the Spirit.
intentions: For the Church: that she may live in the communion of love of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. Let us pray to the Lord.
For all who care for creation: that they may see in it the wisdom and delight of God. Let us pray to the Lord.
For those who suffer: that their suffering may produce endurance, character and a hope that does not disappoint. Let us pray to the Lord.
For theologians and teachers of the faith: that the Spirit may guide them into all truth. Let us pray to the Lord.
For ourselves: that we may live as people loved by the Father, saved by the Son and filled with the Spirit. Let us pray to the Lord.
prayerOfTheFaithful.conclusion: God our Father, you sent your Son and your Spirit to reveal to us the mystery of your life. Help us to worship you, one God in three Persons, and to live in your love. Through Christ our Lord.

reflection.title: God's love poured into our hearts
reflection.body:
The mystery of the Trinity is beyond our understanding, but it is not cold or abstract. It tells us that God is love, an eternal communion of Father, Son and Holy Spirit, and that we are invited into that love.

The Book of Proverbs speaks of God's Wisdom as present at the creation of the world: "When he established the heavens, I was there." Wisdom was beside God "as the craftsman," and she says, "I was a delight day by day, always rejoicing before him." And then something moving: "My delight was with the sons of men." Christians have long heard in these words a hint of the eternal Son, through whom all things were made, who delights in being with us.

The psalm wonders at our place in creation: "what is man, that you think of him?" And yet God has "crowned him with glory and honor."

Paul shows how the three Persons work in our salvation. Through faith "we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ." We have hope, "and hope doesn't disappoint us, because God's love has been poured into our hearts through the Holy Spirit who was given to us." He even says that suffering can lead to hope, through endurance and proven character.

In the Gospel, Jesus speaks of the Spirit who will lead the disciples further: "I still have many things to tell you, but you can't bear them now. However, when he, the Spirit of truth, has come, he will guide you into all truth." And he shows the unity of the three: "All things that the Father has are mine," and the Spirit "will take from what is mine and will declare it to you."

This week, pray the Glory Be slowly each day, giving thanks to the Father who made you, the Son who saved you, and the Spirit who lives in you.
